chapter_name: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
learning_objective: 🎯 Organize the tree of life! Understand why and how scientists group millions of living organisms into Kingdoms using physical and genetic similarities.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: There are millions of species on Earth. Studying them one by one is impossible. Classification groups them by similarities and evolutionary history, making them easier to study and identify.

Invented by Carl Linnaeus. Every species gets a two-part scientific name in Latin: the Genus (capitalized) and the Species (lowercase). E.g., Humans are *Homo sapiens*. Mango is *Mangifera indica*. This avoids confusion across languages.

Life is divided into 5 huge groups: Monera (bacteria, no nucleus), Protista (single-celled with nucleus), Fungi (mushrooms, absorb food), Plantae (plants, make food), and Animalia (animals, eat food).

Divided into groups based on body design and seeds. Thallophyta (algae), Bryophyta (mosses, no roots), Pteridophyta (ferns), Gymnosperms (naked seeds like pine trees), and Angiosperms (flowering plants with hidden seeds).
Divided into Invertebrates (no backbone: sponges, worms, insects) and Vertebrates (with backbone: Fish, Amphibians, Reptiles, Birds, Mammals). Mammals give birth to live young and produce milk.

fun_activity.title: 🏷️ Be a Taxonomist
fun_activity.instructions: Look at a dog, a cat, and a human. How are they grouped? They are all Animalia (kingdom), Chordata (have spinal cords), Mammalia (have hair, make milk). But then they split! Dog = Canidae family, Cat = Felidae family, Human = Hominidae family. Trace your pet's full scientific lineage online!

exam_tips: 📌 Always underline or italicize scientific names (e.g., <u>Panthera tigris</u>). Genus gets a capital letter, species gets a lowercase letter.
📌 Learn the defining characteristics of the 5 Kingdoms. Monera is unique because it's the only one with Prokaryotic (no true nucleus) cells.
📌 Arthropoda is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom (includes all insects, spiders, crabs) characterized by jointed legs and an exoskeleton.
quick_recap: ⭐ Classification reflects evolutionary relationships—organisms in the same group share a common ancestor.
⭐ Fungi were once thought to be plants, but they cannot perform photosynthesis; they are saprophytes (eat dead organic matter).
⭐ The hierarchy of classification: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. (Hint: Keep Pond Clean Or Frog Gets Sick).
